What is the name of the business?
Which country does the business operate in?

help_text.en: This affects tax, advertising rules and data protection requirements.

prompt.en: What type of business is this?
In a few sentences, what does the business do?
What does the business sell?

help_text.en: Select everything that applies.

prompt.en: Which of those brings in the most money?
What stage is the business in right now?
When did the business start operating?

help_text.en: An approximate month is fine.

prompt.en: What is your main focus right now?
How many people work in the business, including you?
How would you describe the size of the business?

help_text.en: Your own sense of it, not a headcount rule. I use it to decide how much detail is worth showing you.

prompt.en: Is the business online, physical, or both?
How many physical locations are there?
What kind of place is it?
Do customers come to this location?
What are the opening hours?

help_text.en: Per day, as you'd write it on the door — e.g. Mon–Thu 20:00–01:00, Fri–Sat 18:00–02:00, Sun closed.

prompt.en: Roughly what does one hour of being open cost you — staff on shift plus energy?

help_text.en: A rough figure is fine. It tells us whether your first and last hours pay for themselves.

prompt.en: What limits how much you can serve? For example seats, appointments per day, or storage space.
What is your website address?
Can customers buy directly on the website?
Which platforms do you sell or publish on?
Do you sell locally, nationally or internationally?
What is the website mainly for?
List what the business sells.

help_text.en: Add each product or service. You can start with the main ones and add more later.

prompt.en: Which one sells the most?
Which one has the best profit margin?
Which one do you most want to grow?
Do you hold stock of your physical products?
How do you track stock levels?
How often do you restock?
Which products run out most often?
Which products sell slowly or are sitting unsold?

help_text.en: Money tied up in slow stock is one of the most common hidden problems.

prompt.en: What does storage cost you per month?
Roughly what is your damaged, expired or dead stock worth?

help_text.en: Enter 0 if there is none.

prompt.en: How do products reach the customer if you don't hold stock?
Who supplies your products?
Do you make or customise the products yourself?
How much can you produce per week?
What is the main thing slowing production down?
Do you ship products to customers?
Which carriers do you use?
Who pays for shipping?
What goes wrong with returns, or lost and damaged parcels, if anything?
Do you deliver locally yourself?
What are the main problems with local delivery?
Walk me through how a service is delivered, from first contact to finish.
Do customers book appointments?
How do they book, and with which tool?
How many appointments can you handle per week?
How much of a problem are no-shows and late cancellations, if at all?
Could someone else deliver the service if you were unavailable?

help_text.en: This is one of the biggest risks in a service business.

prompt.en: How do you keep service quality consistent?
What kind of digital product is it?
What stage is the product in?
How many registered users are there?
How many are paying?
What is your monthly churn rate, if you know it?
Why do users usually cancel?
What is it built on and where is it hosted?
Which bugs or missing features are holding growth back, if any?
Is money coming into the business at the moment?

help_text.en: Any sales at all, even if the business is not making a profit yet.

prompt.en: Roughly how much revenue per month?
How many sales or orders per month?
Is revenue growing, stable or declining?
Roughly what share of customers buy again?
Which was your best month and which was your worst, and roughly how much?

help_text.en: This gives me two points to work from even without full records.

prompt.en: Is the business seasonal?
What is missing before you can start selling?
How do you plan to get your first customers?
Why did the business stop making money?
How do customers pay?
Which payment provider do you use?
What is your refund policy?
Have you changed your prices? What changed and why?
Do you feel your prices are too low, too high, or about right?
What does the business pay every month regardless of sales?

help_text.en: Rent, salaries, software, insurance, loans, subscriptions and so on.

prompt.en: Which costs go up when you sell more, beyond the delivery cost you already gave per product?
What is your gross profit margin?

help_text.en: The percentage of each sale left after the direct cost of delivering it. If you have never worked it out, say you don't know.

prompt.en: Do you have cash flow problems or late-paying customers?
How much debt or financing is the business carrying?

help_text.en: Enter 0 if there is none. Loans, credit lines, buy-now-pay-later on stock, investor money to repay.

prompt.en: Where do you think money is being wasted?
Can you upload any financial records? Revenue reports, a profit and loss statement, or a pricing sheet.
Do you sell to consumers, to businesses, or both?
What problem are customers trying to solve when they come to you?
What makes people hesitate before buying?
Describe your typical customer. Age, location, anything relevant.
What kind of companies buy from you, and who decides?
Of the deals you go after with other businesses, roughly what percentage do you win?

help_text.en: A rough share is fine: if you win about one in four, that's 25. Your pipeline uses it to weigh open deals until it has enough closed ones of its own to measure.

prompt.en: Are there clearly different types of customer?
How do customers usually find you?
How long does it take them to decide to buy?
Do customers recommend you to others?
Do you keep a list of customer contacts anywhere?

help_text.en: Even a spreadsheet counts.

prompt.en: Roughly how many contacts?
Do you have permission to email those contacts for marketing?

help_text.en: This matters legally before anything is sent.

prompt.en: Where do your sales come from?
Which is your main sales channel?
Which channel is underperforming?
What happens between someone first hearing about you and actually paying?
Do you use any sales materials? Scripts, proposals, price lists, landing pages, testimonials.
Do you run paid advertising?
How much do you spend on ads per month?
What's the most you'd want to spend on ads in a month?

help_text.en: A ceiling, not a target. SYB never proposes raising an ad budget past it.

prompt.en: Which platforms do you advertise on?
Roughly what does it cost you to get one sale from ads?
What happened when you advertised before, and why did you stop?
Do you post content anywhere?

help_text.en: Social media, video, a blog, a newsletter — anything you publish yourself.

prompt.en: How often do you post?
What content has worked best so far?
Which social accounts does the business have? Please include the handles.
Do you have a logo and brand colours?
If you had one sentence to tell someone why to choose you, what would it be?
What should customers feel about the brand?
Who is the face of the business, if anyone?
Do you collect email addresses or leads from people who don't buy immediately?
Where can people read reviews or testimonials about you, if anywhere?
Is the business operating normally right now?
Describe a normal working day in the business.
What takes up the most time each week?
What goes wrong most often?
Who works in the business and what do they do?
What do you personally spend most of your time on?
How do customers contact you when they have a problem?
Is there a set way of handling customer questions, or is it ad hoc?
What do customers ask about most often?
What do customers complain about most often?
Are any of your processes written down as instructions or checklists?
Which part of running the business causes you the most stress?
Which tools and software do you use to run the business?

help_text.en: Website, payments, accounting, bookings, email, spreadsheets, anything.

prompt.en: Which of these areas do you already have a tool for?
Do you have any automations set up already?

help_text.en: Automatic emails, order syncing, scheduled posts, anything that runs on its own.

prompt.en: Which of these do you still do by hand?
If one task could disappear tomorrow, which would it be?
What numbers do you already track, and where do they live?
Could you export that data if needed?
What legal form is the business?
What is your VAT status?
Which licences, permits or insurance does the business need to operate, if any?
Do you have terms and conditions and a privacy policy published?
What postal address should appear at the foot of your marketing emails?

help_text.en: The US and Canada require a real postal address in every marketing email; elsewhere it's good practice. A PO box you check is fine.

prompt.en: Which single platform or account could the business not survive losing, if any?
What could stop the business tomorrow?
What advertising or industry restrictions apply in your field, if any?

help_text.en: For example age limits, health claims, or regulated products.

prompt.en: Who are your main competitors?

help_text.en: Names and links are enough to start. I'll research the rest.

prompt.en: What makes you different from them?
What proof do you have that it's true? Reviews, results, numbers.
Where are competitors clearly better than you?
Is demand in your market growing, stable or shrinking?
Do customers in your market shop mainly on price?
What do you want to achieve in the next 3, 6 and 12 months?
What is the single biggest thing stopping growth right now?
What have you already tried to grow the business?
What failed, and why do you think it failed?
What should definitely not be tried again, if anything?
Are you planning any of these?
What would you never want the business to do, regardless of results?

help_text.en: Tone, tactics, platforms, discounting. I will treat these as hard limits.

prompt.en: Upload anything you already have that could be useful.

help_text.en: Photos, logo, videos, price lists, reviews, reports. More material means better output later.

prompt.en: Which of these do you have available, even if not uploaded yet?

localisation.policy: Additional locales added after Gate 1, chosen by where paying customers actually come from. Not decided in advance.
